title: Rex Stewart and Harlem after hours
summary: Greer recalls Rex Stewart in Fletcher's band and Harlem all-night life where white musicians came to learn.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Did you meet any of the musicians who were later to be in the band in Washington other than Hardwick?

Oh, yeah, Rex. How could I forget Rex. He was from Washington. But he was already in New York. Playing with Fletcher. He was playing with Fletcher. He played with Fletcher when we was down at the Kentucky Club, but we all used to hang out in Harlem after we'd leave the club. If you went home before 9:00 in the morning, you was an amateur. See our guys, all the tuxedos, at 8:00 in the morning, 9:00 in the morning. See the women all fancied, 9:00 in the morning. Harlem was heaven, that was the name of Harlem then, it was heaven, you know.

If you didn't make the scene, because all the faces would come down, all the musicians, white ones, all of them, Tommy Dorsey, Jimmy and all of them, the whole crowd. Red Nichols, all of them. Red Nichols played down the corner from us, from the Kentucky Club.
